title: Sojourner
tagline: The little rover who went first. Mars, 1997.
mystery: Who drove the first wheels on Mars? And is it still there?
p1.date: Mars. 4 July 1997. Something is falling from the sky…
p1.bounce: Wrapped in airbags, it bounced at least 15 times. The first bounce was as high as a four-storey building!
p1.petals: Its metal petals open like a flower. Something small is riding inside.
p2.hello: Hello, Mars! My name is Sojourner.
p2.size: I am no bigger than a microwave oven. But I have a very big job.
p2.wheels: My wheels are the first wheels ever to roll on another planet!
p3.slow: My top speed is one centimetre a second. A tortoise would win!
p3.delay: Earth is so far away that a message takes more than 10 minutes to reach me.
p3.plan: So nobody can steer me. Plan my path, then send it!
p3.goal: Plan a path to the first rock
p3.hint: Tap the ground to add stops. Stay clear of the red rings. Then press SEND.
p3.win: Your plan flew across space, and I followed every step!
p4.names: My team named these rocks after cartoon characters!
p4.apxs: My sensor can tell what a rock is made of. Pick a rock!
p4.hint: Tap a rock's name. When I get there, hold the button until the bar is full.
p4.barnacleBill: Barnacle Bill is made like andesite, a rock from volcanoes. Nobody expected that!
p4.yogi: Yogi wears a coat of dust. Under the dust, it is a lot like Barnacle Bill.
p4.scoobyDoo: Scooby-Doo is almost the same as the soil around it.
p4.win: I told Earth what the rocks of Mars are made of!
p5.look: Wait. Some of these stones look different. Can you spot them?
p5.hint: Tap the stones that look like pebbles from a river. Sharp rocks do not count.
p5.miss: Too sharp! Look for smooth ones.
p5.water: Smooth and round, like pebbles in a river!
p5.wet: That is a clue. Long ago, water may have flowed right here on Mars.
p6.plan: The plan: Sojourner would work for just 7 days.
p6.hint: Tap fast. How far past the plan can Sojourner go?
p6.win: Every morning I asked for one more day. I worked for 83!
p6.far: I drove about 100 metres, and never went farther than 12 metres from my lander.
p7.blue: A sunset on Mars is blue. That is real: fine dust in the air makes it so.
p7.quiet: On 27 September 1997 the lander went quiet. It was the little rover's only way to call home.
p7.hello: Hello? … Earth? … Can anybody hear me?
p7.backup: My backup plan was to circle the lander and wait. Maybe I did. Nobody on Earth knows.
p8.sad: Do not be sad for me.
p8.after: After me came Spirit and Opportunity. Then Curiosity. Then Perseverance.
p8.tracks: I went first, so that they could go far.
p9.done: My part is done. For Mars, and for the Earth.
p9.still: Sojourner is still there today, in a valley called Ares Vallis.
p9.next: Next signal: the rover that would not stop…
